answer: Admission is capped at 3 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm thus spreads across origins and burns for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the orchard quota and the jade admission check. Because the ocean audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
